newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN OLOS, SUPPLY OUT OF WAY, TO WAIT FOR US DATA.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN OLOS, SUPPLY OUT OF WAY, TO WAIT FOR US DATA.

text.p: The Belgian OLO market, with 23 billion francs of supply from Monday's auction safely under its belt, will wait for U.S. data later in the week before its next move, dealers said.

While coupon payments could provide some near term support, the prospect of the monthly U.S. jobs report on Friday would keep investors sidelined. OLO 16 will on Tuesday pay out around 20.8 billion francs in coupons. That will be followed on Wednesday with 29.7 billion francs from OLO 11.
The curve flattening move seen last week on fears about short term rates had probably run its course for now, they said.

European bonds ended off their lows as U.S. Treasuries, buoyed by a surging dollar, edged higher in early trade. The benchmark 10-year OLO 26 yielded 5.65 percent in late trade, just one basis point higher than late Friday and below levels at the Treasury's monthly auction held earlier.

The Treasury said earlier it had sold 10.035 billion francs of OLO 26 at an average yield of 5.67 percent. It also sold 13.020 billion francs of OLO 14 at a yield of 5.20 percent. OLO 14 had recovered to yield 5.18 percent by the close. The Treasury will hold a non-competitive auction in each bond on Tuesday.
"Levels (at the auction) looked fair to me, but there was not really any demand," one trader said.

Another said end-investors had expressed an interest in the paper on offer. "But not that many," he added, noting the uncertainty weighing on the market because of Friday's U.S. data. "It's going to be very nervous till then," he said.

Meanwhile, the ballooning of money market rates that started two weeks ago and accelerated last week with talk of a possible Bundesbank rate hike to support the mark continued, pushing both Belgian treasury bill yields and repo rates higher.
The National Bank of Belgium (NBB) provided no support to the market, cutting liquidity at its weekly tender to seven from 10 billion Belgian francs.
One week repos ended at 4.05/15 percent and upwards compared with late Friday levels around 3.90/00 percent.

One money market trader said three-month treasury bill yields at Tuesday's auction would correspondingly suffer, rising from last week's 3.43 percent level to leave the yield curve inverted -- with three month bills more expensive than six or 12-months. -- Nick Antonovics, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6817, Fax +32 2 230 7710
